title: Importance of Bridging Loans for Property Development
summary: Blog article (not a case study). Thesis as revealed by search snippets only: property bridging loans play a role in the UK market by giving borrowers fast, flexible funds; developers use them to cover funding gaps so a project stays on schedule; bridging loans are described as tools that cover a funding need until future income arrives, used by both investors and developers; the article notes they usually carry higher interest than conventional mortgages, reflecting their short-term nature and higher risk. No full text, no headings, no worked examples, no figures were returned for this page. A mirror of the same article exists on the firm's Wix blog (https://silveroakcapitaluk.wixsite.com/blogs/post/bridging-loan-for-property-development, titled 'Importance Of Bridging Loan For Property Development'). Related Silver Oak pages surfaced in search (b) add context from sibling pages, not from this article: developers use bridging to buy a site before long-term finance is in place and to refinance a near-complete project; usual duration roughly 6 to 24 months (/how-does-a-bridge-loan-work-for-developers/); a bridge lets a developer secure a site quickly while full development finance is still being arranged, land-backed bridges often cap at around 50-60% LTV, and Silver Oak can add mezzanine or equity to reduce the deposit needed (/post-planning-land-acquisitions/).
